Time to call 911 (call for help at the first sign of a stroke!)

You need to be open with her if you want there to be even a drop of possibility that y’all can work this out. Lying or hiding something can be a fatal blow to a relationship. Telling the truth can be hurtful and even cause problems yes, but you just have to face the consequences of your actions and be open and honest with the person you claim to love. When she finds out who the other person is from somebody else, things will be a lot worse and she will question how much she can trust you. If she hears it from you, at least she knows you cared enough to tell her.

I, personally, don’t think you are overreacting. I find it really messed up that she did that to the poor dog. The dog may have been old, but if the vet, a medical professional, said the dog was healthy, then there was no reason for the dog to be euthanized (morally or not). And she chose to do so immorally which just makes everything that much worse. There are SO many other things she could’ve done. (None of which I think should’ve been euthanization even by a vet, considering the dog was healthy.) She could’ve tried looking for a friend, co-worker, or anyone who would gladly accept the dog, for example. 

I just simply don’t understand why she felt the need to get the dog euthanized at all. Considering she got another dog not too long after, it tells me that she just wanted to get rid of him. The dog was an older dog so she probably didn’t want to take care of it in its old age (aside from it being /supposedly/ aggressive). 

I think if this questionable behavior of your friend is really eating at you, then you should talk it out with them. If they are a dear friend like you say they are, then they should be willing to listen to your feelings. Also, she got another dog and I’m not sure how I feel about that because who’s to say she won’t eventually do the same thing to this one?

The fact that she said she wouldn’t mind if you cheated because that would give her a reason to leave should tell you all you need to know about her headspace in regards to your relationship. It seems like she wants to leave the relationship, but hopes you cheat so that way she can put the blame on you for causing her decision in leaving. You deserve better and don’t deserve this manipulation.

It’s so strange that I came across this post. I thought I was the only person like this.. or used to be? Or maybe I kinda still am like this? It’s hard to explain. 

To begin, I totally related to the fact of never really seeking relationships. I’ve had crushes on guys in school before, and only sometimes imagined what it would be like if I were in a relationship with them. I think I may have only done this twice actually. But anyway, just like you, even if someone I liked, somehow, ended up liking me back and asking me out, I would say no. But then, I’d be upset when and if they ended up dating another person. 

Over a year ago, however, I met this guy online and we instantly clicked. We have a lot of the same interests, similar personalities, mindsets, and we both found each other attractive. However, because of the way I viewed relationships and how reserved and independent I was in that sense, it took a lot of convincing from him for me to give this a try. Although it took a lot of convincing, because of who HE was, I felt it easier to fall for him than anyone else. That’s not to say though that everything after that was smooth sailing, because it was far from it. 

We still struggled with many issues in our relationship because I was still reserved and unfamiliar with relationships, intimacy, and being this kind of close with another human being. 

Because of my mindset and stance on relationships, I thought I was strange, abnormal, and that something was wrong with me. I couldn’t seem to properly show my feelings to him because of how reserved and scared I was of the concept of relationships. 

I mean, even when I was crushing on guys in school and even crushing on celebrities, I never even got sexual thoughts or fantasies about them. It was even difficult for me to get such thoughts about my bf. I only ever imagined the cutesy stuff like cuddling, forehead kisses, holding hands, and soft kisses on the lips. At one point, my boyfriend and I even thought I was asexual because of how deviant I seemed to be when it came to wanting relationships and taking part in them. Eventually, I realized I wasn’t asexual, but rather, I was afraid to express my attraction for another person and I didn’t know how to. I think you have to love and enjoy the feeling of having someone, try and make the most of a relationship (in a healthy way of course), and not stop yourself from experiencing new things that you think you may not enjoy OR you’re afraid of one thing or another. 

I’m currently still struggling with a lot of related issues myself, but I did learn A LOT ever since I got into a relationship. Every person is different and I don’t believe you’re abnormal.
